surprises.description: Q3 adjusted net revenue was $1.4 billion, about 12% above the preview’s $1.25 billion consensus estimate—a substantial beat on the line the preview considered beatable but not decisive.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adjusted net revenue | Q3 FY26 Consensus | $1.25B”; “Consensus revenue of $1.25B looks beatable.”

surprises.description: SoFi raised its FY26 adjusted net revenue outlook to $5.4 billion, far above the prior $4.75–$4.85 billion range the preview used; this was a much larger upward reset than the preview’s bull case of raising revenue above $4.90 billion.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Management raised full-year 2026 guidance to $5.4 billion in adjusted net revenue (up 40%), well above the prior $4.75-$4.85 billion range.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY guide $4.75–4.85B”; bull case: “FY revenue raised above $4.90B.”

surprises.description: Q3 adjusted EBITDA reached $470 million, above the preview’s estimated $430–$450 million range and its description of roughly $430 million as the whisper. This also cleared the preview’s key concern that EBITDA might fall short of the ramp needed for the full-year target.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Record adjusted EBITDA of $470 million at a 34% margin.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Adj. EBITDA (est. to stay on FY track) | ~$430–450M”; “Adj. EBITDA vs. ~$430M whisper — the real number that matters.”

surprises.description: The FY26 EBITDA outlook rose to $1.66 billion rather than merely holding near the preview’s roughly $1.6 billion expectation. The increase is more modest than the revenue-guide reset, but it answers the preview’s main concern about whether the EBITDA ramp would be maintained.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Adjusted EBITDA of $1.66 billion” in the raised full-year guidance.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “FY26 EBITDA guidance language — reaffirmed at ~$1.6B, trimmed, or raised”; the base case expected EBITDA “held at ~$1.6B.”

surprises.description: SoFi issued a strong preliminary 2027 outlook—$6.4 billion revenue, $2.24 billion adjusted EBITDA and $0.90 EPS—where the preview discussed a 2027 bridge but gave no such company outlook. Management also said this growth can be funded organically, without raising additional capital.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SoFi issued preliminary 2027 guidance of $6.4 billion in revenue (27% growth), $2.24 billion adjusted EBITDA (~35% margin), $1.28 billion net income, and $0.90 EPS, stating it can be funded organically without raising additional capital.”

surprises.description: Member growth outpaced the preview’s expected Q3 level: 17.1 million compares with its estimate of about 16.7–16.9 million, implying roughly 1.3 million net adds from Q2’s 15.8 million rather than the expected 0.9–1.1 million.

The personal-loan all-in net charge-off rate was 3.4%, above the preview’s roughly 3.0% threshold for a credit deterioration concern, even though the reported rate improved year over year. This is a negative versus the preview’s focus on credit remaining below that level.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The all-in personal loan net charge-off rate improved to 3.4%, down roughly 80 basis points year-over-year.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “A reversal above ~3.0% … would validate the ‘multiple compresses to 8–10x like a traditional lender’ bear thesis”; the catalyst checklist says breaking back above 3% would re-rate the stock as a subprime lender.

surprises.description: Technology Platform’s reported revenue decline was broadly in line with the preview’s expectation of a third consecutive decline, but the explanation and underlying trend were less damaging than that warning implied: revenue grew 18% excluding the lost large client, and management expects a return to 25% growth.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Technology Platform revenue fell 24% YoY to $87 million due to the loss of a large client, though it grew 18% excluding that client, and management expects a return to 25% growth.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Technology Platform, which has declined two straight quarters (−23% YoY in Q2, −27% in Q1) — a third decline undercuts the platform narrative.”

surprises.description: SoFi Plus had only about 275,000 subscribers in Q3, and management said subscriber growth was below expectations because of execution issues. The preview highlighted the ambition to reach 1 million subscribers but did not anticipate a current-quarter shortfall or execution problems; management said the issues are fixed and reaffirmed the 1 million target for end-2027.
surprises.fact_evidence: “SoFi Plus subscriber growth came in below expectations at ~275,000 in Q3 due to execution issues now said to be fixed, with management reaffirming a target of 1 million subscribers by the end of 2027.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Plus hit 200k paid members in its first quarter”; Noto: “I'd be disappointed if we are not at 1 million SoFi Plus members … a year from now.”
